mainTopic: The end of the first משנה in יבמות (how עריות exempt their צרות, and the limits of that rule) and the גמרא's question about the order of the list
overview: This amud finishes the first משנה of יבמות and begins the גמרא. The משנה completes its list of fifteen עריות and rules that each one frees her צרה, and even the צרה's צרה, from both יבום and חליצה forever. It limits this rule: if the ערוה died, did מיאון, was divorced, or turned out to be an איילונית before the brother died, her co-wives are permitted. It also notes that איילונית and מיאון cannot apply to the women who are forbidden because they are mothers, such as a mother-in-law. The משנה then gives worked examples of how the exemption passes from co-wife to co-wife, even through a hundred brothers, and of when it never starts at all. It adds a middle case: if the ערוה could have done מיאון but did not, her co-wife does חליצה but not יבום. The גמרא then asks why the list does not start with אחות אשה, the source case. It suggests the list is ordered by severity, following רבי שמעון, but rejects that idea. It concludes that בתו comes first because her איסור is learned from a דרשה and is dear to the תנא.

steps.title: The last two women on the list
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of fifteen forbidden relatives with the wife of a brother who never lived at the same time as him, and his daughter-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the wife of his brother who was not alive in the world together with him, and his daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה names the last two women in its list of fifteen עריות. If one of them falls to the surviving brother for יבום, he cannot marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case is אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו: the brother died before the surviving brother was born. The מצוה of יבום does not cover this case, so she stays forbidden as an ordinary אשת אח. The second case is his daughter-in-law (כלתו), who later married his brother. She is a ערוה to him whether or not יבום applies.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of a brother who died before this brother was born
A woman forbidden to a man as a close relative

phrases.english: And the wife of his brother
who was not in the world with him,
phrases.notes: Literally 'was not in his world.' The brother died before this brother was even born.

phrases.english: and his daughter-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of fifteen עריות, which began earlier on the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wife of a brother who did not live at the same time as him, and his daughter-in-law, are the last two עריות on the list

steps.title: These women free their co-wives forever
steps.stepSummary: All fifteen women exempt their co-wives, and the co-wives of those co-wives, from both חליצה and יבום, with no end to the chain.
steps.simpleTranslation: These women exempt their co-wives, and the co-wives of their co-wives, from חליצה and from יבום until the end of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the list is complete, the משנה states the main rule. Each of these women frees her צרה (her co-wife from the same husband) from both יבום and חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a widow with no children needs either יבום or חליצה. Here, the ערוה makes her co-wife just as forbidden as she is. The rule also passes down a chain: a co-wife of that co-wife, from another marriage, is also exempt, without limit. That is the meaning of 'until the end of the world.'

keyTerms.meaning: A co-wife, another wife of the same husband
The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
Levirate marriage, when a brother marries his childless brother's widow

steps.whatToRemember: The ערוה does not just keep herself out of יבום. She frees her co-wife, and the co-wife's co-wife, from both יבום and חליצה forever.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main rule of the first פרק of יבמות. The rest of the sugya will look for where in the Torah this rule comes from.

phrases.english: These exempt
their co-wives and the co-wives of their co-wives
from release (chalitza) and from levirate marriage
until the end of the world.
phrases.notes: He means forever: however long the chain of co-wives gets, each one is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ פּוֹטְרוֹת צָרוֹתֵיהֶן וְצָרוֹת צָרוֹתֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the rule that applies to the whole list just completed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the fifteen עריות exempts her co-wives, and their co-wives, from both חליצה and יבום forever

steps.title: When the co-wives are not exempt
steps.stepSummary: If the ערוה was no longer the brother's wife when he died, her co-wives are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for all of them: if they died, or refused, or were divorced, or were found to be an איילונית, their co-wives are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits the rule it just gave. The exemption only works if the ערוה was still married to the brother at the moment he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In four cases she is not his wife at the time of death. She may have died before him. She may have done מיאון, which cancels a marriage made while she was a minor. She may have been divorced. Or she may turn out to be an איילונית, which makes the marriage a mistake from the start. In each case nothing connects her to the co-wife when יבום comes into effect, so the co-wife is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: They did מיאון, a minor girl's refusal that cancels her marriage
A woman who never develops physically and cannot have children

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'permitted' means the co-wife is back under the normal laws of יבום. She may go to יבום, or the brother does חליצה. It does not mean she is free to marry anyone without חליצה.

phrases.english: And all of them, if they died
or refused,
phrases.notes: A girl married off as a minor by her mother or brothers can cancel the marriage by refusing it.

phrases.english: or were divorced
or were found to be an aylonit
phrases.notes: Her marriage counts as a mistake, as if it never happened.

phrases.english: their co-wives are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of step 2 to cases where the ערוה was married to the brother when he died
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the ערוה died, did מיאון, was divorced, or was an איילונית, her co-wives are permitted

steps.title: Two exceptions that cannot apply to some women
steps.stepSummary: The משנה notes that איילונית and מיאון cannot apply to a mother-in-law, her mother, or the father-in-law's mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you cannot say about his mother-in-law, his mother-in-law's mother, or his father-in-law's mother that they were found to be an איילונית or that they refused.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה comments on its own wording. 'All of them' in step 3 is not fully exact, because two of the four exceptions cannot happen to some women on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three women are only forbidden to him because they are mothers. An איילונית cannot have children, so she could never become anyone's mother-in-law. מיאון is done only by a minor girl, and the משנה treats her as someone who could not have given birth. So only death and divorce can apply to these three women.

keyTerms.meaning: But you cannot say, introducing a limit on the wording

steps.whatToRemember: The four exceptions apply to the list in general. For the women who are forbidden because they are mothers, only death and divorce are possible.

phrases.english: But you cannot say
regarding his mother-in-law and his mother-in-law's mother
and his father-in-law's mother
that they were found to be an aylonit
phrases.notes: An איילונית can't have children, so she could never be someone's mother-in-law.

phrases.english: or that they refused.
phrases.notes: Only a minor girl can refuse, and she hasn't had children, so this can't fit a mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the word 'all of them' in step 3 for three women on the list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איילונית and מיאון cannot apply to his mother-in-law, her mother, or his father-in-law's mother, since all three must be mothers

steps.title: How a forbidden relative exempts her co-wife, and her co-wife's co-wife
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a concrete case: a man's daughter is married to his brother, who has another wife and dies. The daughter is exempt, so her co-wife is exempt too. If that co-wife later marries a second brother who dies, her own co-wife is also exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do they exempt their co-wives? Say his daughter, or any of these forbidden women, was married to his brother. That brother had another wife and died. Just as his daughter is exempt, so is her co-wife. If the daughter's co-wife then married his second brother, who had another wife and died, then just as the daughter's co-wife is exempt, so is her co-wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is explaining its earlier rule from Step 2 by walking through a real-life example of how the exemption passes from one wife to the next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter is forbidden to her father, the surviving brother, so she is exempt from יבום. Her צרה is exempt along with her. That exempt צרה then passes the same exemption to her own co-wife in a later marriage, so the chain keeps going.

keyTerms.meaning: A co-wife, another wife of the same husband
Exempt, here from both יבום and חליצה
The co-wife of her co-wife, the next link in the chain
His daughter, used as the main example of an ערוה

phrases.english: How do they exempt their co-wives?
If his daughter, or one
phrases.notes: "His" means the surviving brother, the one who would have done the יבום.

phrases.english: of all these forbidden relatives
was married to his brother,
and he had another wife, and he died
just as his daughter is exempt,
so too her co-wife is exempt.
If his daughter's co-wife went
and married his second brother,
and he had another wife, and he died
just as his daughter's co-wife is exempt,
so too her co-wife's co-wife is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a worked example of the rule stated in Step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A co-wife of an ערוה is exempt, and a co-wife of that co-wife is also exempt.

steps.title: The chain continues without limit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that the chain of exemption keeps going, even through a hundred brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if they are a hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one short line saying the pattern from Step 5 never stops, no matter how many links there are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 showed two links in the chain. This line makes clear that the number does not matter. Each exempt co-wife passes the exemption on to the next one.

keyTerms.meaning: One hundred, meaning any number at all

phrases.english: Even if they are a hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands Step 5's two-link example to an unlimited chain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exemption of co-wives continues through any number of brothers.

steps.title: When the forbidden relative left the marriage first, her co-wife is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains Step 3 with a case: if the daughter died or was divorced before the brother died, her co-wife is not exempt and is permitted for יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does it work that if they died, their co-wives are permitted? Say his daughter, or any of these forbidden women, was married to his brother, who had another wife. Then his daughter died or was divorced, and only afterward his brother died. Her co-wife is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is explaining its earlier rule from Step 3 with an example, showing when the chain of exemption does not start at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is the moment the brother dies. If the ערוה is no longer his wife at that point, the other woman is not a co-wife of an ערוה. So she is treated like any normal widow who falls to יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: And afterward, the order of events is what matters

steps.confusionAlert: Only the timing matters. The daughter must die or be divorced BEFORE the brother dies. If she is still married to him when he dies, her co-wife is exempt.

phrases.english: How so, "if they died,"
their co-wives are permitted?
If his daughter, or one
of all these forbidden relatives
was married to his brother,
and he had another wife,
and his daughter died or was divorced,
and afterward his brother died
her co-wife is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case where the co-wife is exempt (Step 5) to the case where she is permitted, explaining Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the ערוה died or was divorced before the brother's death, her co-wife is permitted for יבום.

steps.title: If she could have refused but did not, her co-wife does חליצה but not יבום
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a middle case: if the ערוה was a minor who could have done מיאון but did not, her co-wife may not do יבום, but she still needs חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And any woman who could have refused and did not refuse: her co-wife does חליצה and does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new in-between ruling about a forbidden relative who was a young girl able to do מיאון but never did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she never did מיאון, she was still the brother's wife when he died, so her co-wife may not do יבום. But since the minor's marriage was one she could have undone, the co-wife is not fully exempt and still needs חליצה. This is neither the full exemption of Step 5 nor the full permission of Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who is able to do מיאון, a minor married off by her mother or brothers

steps.whatToRemember: There are three outcomes for a co-wife: fully exempt (the ערוה was still married at the brother's death), fully permitted (the ערוה died or was divorced first), and the middle case: חליצה but no יבום (the ערוה could have done מיאון but did not).

phrases.english: And any woman who could refuse
phrases.notes: This means the ערוה herself, a young girl who could have ended her marriage by מיאון.

phrases.english: and did not refuse
her co-wife does חליצה
and does not do יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, in-between outcome after the fully exempt case (Step 5) and the fully permitted case (Step 7).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The co-wife of an ערוה who could have done מיאון but did not must do חליצה and may not do יבום.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a weaker marriage, one that could have been undone, creates a weaker exemption, which leads to a middle ruling.

steps.title: Why isn't a wife's sister listed first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the order of the משנה. All the cases are learned from אחות אשה, so the משנה should list her first.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Since we learn all of these cases from a wife's sister, the משנה should list a wife's sister first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by questioning the order of the list in the משנה. It asks why the source case, אחות אשה, is not listed first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that an ערוה is exempt from יבום and also exempts her צרה is learned from the case of אחות אשה. Normally you would expect the source case to be listed first and the cases learned from it to come after. The משנה instead begins with בתו, and that is the problem.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Now, since all of them
phrases.notes: "All of them" means all the עריות listed in the משנה.

phrases.english: we derive from a wife's sister,
let it teach a wife's sister first!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי כּוּלְּהוּ מֵאֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה יָלְפִינַן, לִיתְנֵי אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the משנה by questioning its order.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the list in the משנה, which begins with בתו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source case should be listed first, but אחות אשה, the source of all the cases, appears in the middle of the list.

steps.title: Suggested answer: the list goes by severity, following רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the תנא arranged the cases from most severe to least severe. This would follow רבי שמעון, who holds that שריפה is the harshest death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that the תנא listed the cases in order of severity, then this follows רבי שמעון, who says that burning is more severe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer with the words "if you would say." It is setting up an idea that it will test in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations with one's daughter are punished by שריפה. If שריפה is the harshest death penalty, as רבי שמעון holds, then beginning with בתו makes sense, because the list would run from most severe to least severe.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible answer)
He listed them by severity, most severe first

phrases.english: And if you would say:
the tanna listed them in order of severity,
and it follows Rabbi Shimon,
who says burning is more severe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: תַּנָּא חוּמְרֵי חוּמְרֵי נָקֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible explanation for why the משנה does not begin with אחות אשה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ordering principle: the list goes by severity of punishment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list should begin with the source case, אחות אשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list begins with the harshest punishment, שריפה, following רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Then the mother-in-law should come first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the severity answer. If the order went by severity, חמותו should come first, since the Torah writes שריפה about her directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the משנה should list one's mother-in-law first, since the main source for burning is written about the mother-in-law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the severity answer. It points out that the order still doesn't fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא simply started with the שריפה cases, he should start with חמותו. The Torah states שריפה about her explicitly, and the other שריפה cases are learned from her. Yet בתו comes first, so the severity idea does not explain the order.

phrases.english: If so, let it teach his mother-in-law first,
since the main source for burning is written about his mother-in-law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the severity answer of Step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה's order is explained by severity
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: By that logic חמותו, the primary שריפה case written in the Torah, should be first, not בתו.

steps.title: And the daughter-in-law should come right after
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a second rejection. If the order went by severity, כלתו, whose punishment is סקילה, should come right after חמותו, because stoning is the next harshest punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, after his mother-in-law the משנה should list his daughter-in-law, since after burning, stoning is the most severe!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second problem with the severity answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי שמעון's ranking, סקילה comes right after שריפה. Relations with כלתו are punished by סקילה, so she should follow the שריפה cases. Instead she appears at the end of the list.

phrases.english: And furthermore: after his mother-in-law, let it teach his daughter-in-law,
phrases.notes: In the משנה, כלתו is actually at the very end of the list.

phrases.english: since after burning, stoning is the most severe!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rejection of the severity answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה's order is explained by severity
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The סקילה case, כלתו, should come right after the שריפה cases, but it is placed last.

steps.title: New answer: the daughter is listed first because her case is dear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the severity answer. It explains that בתו comes first because her איסור is learned through a דרשה, which makes it dear to the תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, his daughter is listed first because her prohibition comes from a דרשה, so it is dear to the תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the severity idea and offers a new reason why בתו comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah never states the איסור of one's daughter openly. It is learned through a דרשה. Because this is a new, hard-earned teaching, the תנא cherishes it and puts it at the head of the list.

keyTerms.meaning: From a דרשה, an interpretation of the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Severity alone does not explain why בתו opens the list. She is placed first because her איסור comes from a דרשה, which makes it especially dear to the תנא.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think בתו is a lesser איסור because it comes from a דרשה. It is a full ערוה; the דרשה only explains why she is listed first.

phrases.english: Rather: his daughter, since it comes from an interpretation,
is dear to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בִּתּוֹ, כֵּיוָן דְּאָתְיָא מִדְּרָשָׁא, חַבִּיבָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected severity answer with a new explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New ordering principle: affection for a case learned through a דרשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list is ordered by severity of punishment.
steps.terutzMaskana: בתו is first because her איסור is learned through a דרשה and is dear to the תנא.
